analysis:
The PR adds a documentation section for a 'Model Requant Upload' CI workflow and a new numpy-only re-quantizer, scripts/models/requant.py. The workflow file (.github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml), the manifest-comparison script and the tests were not supplied, so the described controls (master-only ref guard, prod-environment approval, secrets held only by the upload step, byte-for-byte manifest comparison, conditional reservation) are unverified contracts. I cannot confirm that the checks are enforced in code.

Documentation points worth later review:
- The docs state that repository-level R2_* secrets (the default keys=legacy set) stay readable by any workflow a writer pushes, outside the prod gate. The prod environment's branch policy also allows v* branches and tags, and the ref guard works only inside the copy of the workflow being run.
- The default therefore routes model-bucket write credentials through a weaker control. This is documented as a residual, not a new code regression.
- The model bucket is the trust root for provider weights (A-004, T-012, T-027). Mitigations are that promotion is a separate approved step, providers verify file hashes, and the output is compared to a locally qualified manifest.

requant.py itself: it fetches remotely, with a Range length check. The build uses only numpy and does no deserialization of untrusted pickles. It uses tempfile and an exclusive makedirs for the output directory. The path-containment gap in cmd_build's file copy, noted in the finding, is low severity. selftest digests are self-recorded, so selftest is a reproducibility check, not an authenticity check. The authoritative integrity check is the external manifest comparison, which is outside the supplied evidence. No threat model update was identified beyond noting this new publication path as a supply-chain input to A-004.

findings.detail: cmd_build reads the template's manifest.json over the network and, for each entry, opens os.path.join(a.out, p) for writing with no check on p. A path with '..' or an absolute path escapes the output directory. The same applies to tensor-derived filenames from the template's weight map. The docs say only the workflow's input manifest_json and template_url are validated (no '.'/'..' parts). They do not say the fetched template manifest is validated. Likewise get() passes any URL to urllib.urlopen, so a file:// URL or a redirect is accepted if the workflow guard is bypassed. If the model bucket, the CDN or the template content were tampered with, the build job could overwrite files in the runner workspace, including inputs of the later upload step in the secret-bearing prod-environment job. Fix: in the script, reject any p that is not a single safe relative component or that resolves outside a.out. Also restrict the URL scheme to https and the allowed hosts, and validate the fetched manifest the same way as manifest_json.
findings.title: requant.py build writes template-manifest paths to disk without containment or scheme checks
